observations.meaning: Average fused affinity among patients assigned to the same candidate set.

observations.meaning: Algorithmic eigengap screening resolution for each candidate set.
observations.finding: Every set screens at candidate_k=1, meaning the dominant gap sits at the single-cluster resolution; this screening does not indicate a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal within any set.

observations.meaning: Profile of spectral eigengaps across candidate resolutions within each set.
observations.finding: In every set the first eigengap is far larger than all subsequent gaps (subsequent values are on the order of 0.0002 to 0.0027), so the spectral profile is dominated by the single-cluster resolution rather than by any internal multi-cluster structure.

observations.meaning: Relatively close candidate pairs and their average fused affinity across the pair boundary.
observations.finding: The closest pairs (e.g., K8_C0004/K8_C0006, K8_C0002/K8_C0003, K8_C0006/K8_C0008) have between-set affinities around 0.0091 to 0.0093, which is close to the within-set affinity range (about 0.0097 to 0.0104); these pairs are a review entry point, not a merge conclusion.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic describes the fused four-view patient geometry for the eight candidate sets. All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. The spectral screening is uniform: every set has screen_candidate_k=1, and in each set the leading eigengap (about 0.06 to 0.16) is much larger than all subsequent gaps (about 0.0002 to 0.0027). This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. The nearest-pair affinities show that several candidate pairs have between-set affinity close to the within-set range, so the boundaries between those pairs are relatively weak in the fused geometry. Because this tool reports partition-level screening and pair affinities rather than GRV or native-distance label alignment, it does not by itself establish whether the four views share the same candidate boundaries; it characterizes internal structure and boundary proximity in the fused geometry only. Weak pair separation is a review entry point and does not imply that any pair should be merged, and the absence of a dominant internal subdivision signal does not imply that any set should be split.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: No prior Evidence Reports are available for this EvidenceRequest, so this report stands alone and cannot be cross-checked against earlier interpreted evidence.

observations.finding: The down-regulated programs are not independent; they reflect a shared mitochondrial/metabolic axis rather than many distinct biological processes.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: K8_C0001 shows a coherent and interpretable biological phenotype relative to the rest of the partition: a broad, coordinated down-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation and related mitochondrial/metabolic programs (adipogenesis, fatty-acid metabolism, heme metabolism, bile-acid metabolism, protein secretion), with the strongest and most significant signal in OXPHOS (NES -1.97, FDR 0.001). The direction is consistently negative across the significant pathways, and the leading-edge gene overlap indicates these are facets of one shared metabolic axis rather than many independent processes. Up-regulated pathways (pancreas beta cells, EMT, MYC targets, E2F targets, angiogenesis) do not reach FDR below 0.05, so the up-regulated side is weaker and less coherent. The contrast is against a heterogeneous rest of 90 samples drawn from seven other candidate sets, so the phenotype is relative to that mixed background rather than to a single reference group.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The only prior Evidence Report is a partition-level structural diagnostic of the fused four-view geometry. It reported comparable within-set cohesion across all sets and screen_candidate_k=1 for every set, with no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions. That report does not address RNA biology, so it neither corroborates nor conflicts with this enrichment result; the two are complementary, describing geometry and transcriptomic phenotype respectively. No prior biological-support report exists for comparison.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: Several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with the partition geometry, but the magnitudes and the separation of location from dispersion effects vary. In the fused geometry, tissue source site has a significant PERMANOVA location association (q 0.0025) with a small R-squared (0.0497) and no detectable PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.434), indicating a modest location shift without dispersion confounding. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase has the largest location association (R-squared 0.154, q 0.0025) but also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.0285), so its PERMANOVA result may partly reflect dispersion; the large UNKNOWN level (40/103) also limits interpretability. CT slice thickness and CT z-spacing show the strongest distance-regression associations (R-squared 0.136 and 0.142, both q 0.002), indicating that acquisition geometry is associated with CT distances. CT manufacturer has a significant location association (q 0.0067) with a significant dispersion difference (q 0.009), so its location result may partly reflect dispersion, and the Philips level has only 3 observations. CT pixel spacing and study year are significant but with small R-squared values (0.019 and 0.029). CT reconstruction kernel and CT scanner model are only nominally associated (p 0.048 and 0.054) and do not survive correction; their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because of sparse levels. These are association measures, not proof of technical artifact or causation, and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding. The pattern indicates that site and CT acquisition factors are associated with the geometry and warrant consideration, but the small R-squared values for most factors mean they do not by themselves account for a large share of the geometry.

All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. The spectral screening is uniform: every set has screen_candidate_k=1, and in each set the leading eigengap (about 0.06 to 0.16) is much larger than all subsequent gaps (about 0.0002 to 0.0027). This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. The nearest-pair affinities show that several candidate pairs have between-set affinity close to the within-set range, so the boundaries between those pairs are relatively weak in the fused geometry. Because this tool reports partition-level screening and pair affinities rather than GRV or native-distance label alignment, it does not by itself establish whether the four views share the same candidate boundaries; it characterizes internal structure and boundary proximity in the fused geometry only. Weak pair separation is a review entry point and does not imply that any pair should be merged, and the absence of a dominant internal subdivision signal does not imply that any set should be split.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: K8_C0002 shows a mutation profile that is coherent in direction but limited in scope relative to the rest of the partition. TP53 enrichment (3/15 versus 0/88) is significant within the driver panel (q_driver 0.0193) but not globally (q_global 1.0), and the odds-ratio interval is extremely wide (2.41 to 1017), reflecting the small number of events. PBRM1 depletion and KDM5C enrichment have nominal Fisher evidence but do not survive driver-panel correction. The remaining driver genes are either nonsignificant or not estimable. The exploratory non-driver genes with nominal enrichment all rest on 2/15 versus 0/88 and do not survive global correction. evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic describes the fused four-view patient geometry for the eight candidate sets. All sets are populated (7 to 20 patients) and show comparable internal cohesion, with mean within-set affinity tightly clustered near 0.010. The spectral screening is uniform: every set has screen_candidate_k=1, and in each set the leading eigengap (about 0.06 to 0.16) is much larger than all subsequent gaps (about 0.0002 to 0.0027). This pattern indicates that the dominant spectral resolution within each set is the single-cluster resolution; the screening does not reveal a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision signal, and no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions are reported here. The nearest-pair affinities show that several candidate pairs have between-set affinity close to the within-set range, so the boundaries between those pairs are relatively weak in the fused geometry. Because this tool reports partition-level screening and pair affinities rather than GRV or native-distance label alignment, it does not by itself establish whether the four views share the same candidate boundaries; it characterizes internal structure and boundary proximity in the fused geometry only. Weak pair separation is a review entry point and does not imply that any pair should be merged, and the absence of a dominant internal subdivision signal does not imply that any set should be split.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: Among the measured technical, acquisition, and site factors, three show statistically significant association with candidate-set membership after BH correction: tissue source site (Cramér's V 0.258, q=0.003), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.220, q=0.0011), and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.219, q=0.0011). The remaining factors (CT phase, manufacturer, scanner model, reconstruction kernel, pixel spacing, study year) do not survive correction, with pixel spacing and study year showing essentially no association. These are association measures, not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant associations indicate that site and CT acquisition geometry could plausibly account for part of the partition geometry and warrant consideration, while the nonsignificant factors do not establish absence of confounding. The analysis covers 103 observations across the partition.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The only prior Evidence Report is the partition-level structural diagnostic of the fused four-view geometry, which reported comparable within-set cohesion and screen_candidate_k=1 for all sets with no feasible k>=2 solutions. limitations: Association is not causation; significant PERMANOVA-style or Kruskal-Wallis results do not prove that these factors drive the partition.

Nonsignificance for the remaining factors does not establish absence of confounding, particularly given the limited sample size (n=103).

observations.finding: VHL is strongly depleted in K8_C0002 (0/15 mutated versus 56/88 in rest; q_driver 2.76e-05, q_global 0.0066), while TP53 is enriched (3/15 versus 0/88; q_driver 0.0193 but q_global 1.0). evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: K8_C0002 shows a mutation profile that is coherent in direction but limited in scope relative to the rest of the partition. The dominant, multiplicity-robust feature is near-complete absence of VHL mutation (0/15 versus 56/88 in rest), which is significant both within the prespecified driver panel (q_driver 2.76e-05) and across the full interpretation matrix (q_global 0.0066). This is a depletion rather than an enrichment and distinguishes K8_C0002 from the VHL-mutant majority of the partition. TP53 enrichment (3/15 versus 0/88) is significant within the driver panel (q_driver 0.0193) but not globally (q_global 1.0), and the odds-ratio interval is extremely wide (2.41 to 1017), reflecting the small number of events. PBRM1 depletion and KDM5C enrichment have nominal Fisher evidence but do not survive driver-panel correction. The remaining driver genes are either nonsignificant or not estimable. The exploratory non-driver genes with nominal enrichment all rest on 2/15 versus 0/88 and do not survive global correction. Overall, the mutation evidence for K8_C0002 is a single robust depletion (VHL) plus a weaker, panel-level TP53 enrichment, with no broad coordinated mutation signature across the panel.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior RNA pathway enrichment for K8_C0002 reported a strong immune-down/metabolic-up transcriptomic phenotype (allograft rejection NES -2.72, interferon gamma -2.63, OXPHOS +2.56, all FDR 0.001). The VHL depletion is notable because VHL loss is a canonical ccRCC driver, so its absence in this set is a biologically interpretable contrast with the rest of the partition, but it does not directly corroborate the RNA immune/metabolic phenotype. The partition-level structural diagnostic reported comparable within-set cohesion and screen_candidate_k=1 for all sets and does not address mutation biology. The confounder report identified tissue source site and CT acquisition geometry as associated with membership, which is relevant context but does not bear on the mutation profile.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: Several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with the partition geometry, but the magnitudes and the separation of location from dispersion effects vary. In the fused geometry, tissue source site has a significant PERMANOVA location association (q 0.0025) with a small R-squared (0.0497) and no detectable PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.434), indicating a modest location shift without dispersion confounding. In the CT native-distance geometry, CT phase has the largest location association (R-squared 0.154, q 0.0025) but also a significant PERMDISP dispersion difference (q 0.0285), so its PERMANOVA result may partly reflect dispersion; the large UNKNOWN level (40/103) also limits interpretability. CT slice thickness and CT z-spacing show the strongest distance-regression associations (R-squared 0.136 and 0.142, both q 0.002), indicating that acquisition geometry is associated with CT distances. CT manufacturer has a significant location association (q 0.0067) with a significant dispersion difference (q 0.009), so its location result may partly reflect dispersion, and the Philips level has only 3 observations. CT pixel spacing and study year are significant but with small R-squared values (0.019 and 0.029). CT reconstruction kernel and CT scanner model are only nominally associated (p 0.048 and 0.054) and do not survive correction; their PERMDISP tests are not estimable because of sparse levels. These are association measures, not proof of technical artifact or causation, and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding. The pattern indicates that site and CT acquisition factors are associated with the geometry and warrant consideration, but the small R-squared values for most factors mean they do not by themselves account for a large share of the geometry.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior Evidence Reports include a partition-level structural diagnostic of the fused four-view geometry (comparable within-set cohesion, screen_candidate_k=1 for all sets, no feasible k>=2 solutions), RNA pathway enrichment for all eight sets, and WXS mutation enrichment for six sets. The structural diagnostic did not assess technical factors, so this confounder report is complementary: it identifies site and CT acquisition geometry as factors associated with candidate membership, which is relevant context for interpreting the fused geometry and the RNA/WXS contrasts but does not by itself explain or invalidate them. The RNA and WXS reports describe biological phenotypes relative to a heterogeneous rest; the confounder associations mean that part of the geometry separating sets could reflect site or acquisition differences, which is a tension that downstream review should weigh alongside the biological signals. No prior confounder report exists for comparison.

The set-level confounder report shows no significant technical, site, or acquisition association with membership after correction, so the measured factors do not provide a substantial alternative explanation. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable within-set cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision signal, and the nearest-pair affinities are only modestly close. The candidate has an interpretable identity and no material unresolved alternative explanation; the heterogeneous-rest and small-size limitations are acknowledged but do not undermine independent retention.

The RNA report describes a strong, coherent immune-down/metabolic-up phenotype (allograft rejection NES -2.72, interferon gamma -2.63, OXPHOS +2.56, all FDR 0.001), and the WXS report adds a complementary, multiplicity-robust VHL depletion (0/15 vs 56/88, q_global 0.0066) that distinguishes this set from the VHL-mutant majority. The set-level confounder report is uniformly null, so measured technical factors do not provide a substantial alternative explanation. The partition structural diagnostic shows comparable cohesion and no dominant internal subdivision. The TP53 enrichment is panel-level only and the rest group is heterogeneous, but the integrated evidence positively supports an interpretable identity and independent retention.
